scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8872: Users in BOTH pods report the entire data center is
gone: from host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1, every 10.200.0.x address times out,
DNS queries to 10.200.0.2 time out, and no portal loads by name or by IP.
Pod-to-pod traffic between the two user hosts still works. The server team
says the servers themselves are up and can still ping each other and their
gateway 10.200.0.1. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on switch_server_access and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_server_access ospfd
Mechanism: switch_server_access is the server farm's L3 edge: it owns the
  farm gateway 10.200.0.1 on br0 and advertises 10.200.0.0/24 into OSPF
  area 0 over its uplink to router_core_3 (172.16.0.10/31). With ospfd
  killed, zebra flushes its OSPF-learned routes immediately, so replies
  leaving the farm via 10.200.0.1 have no route back to 10.1.1.0/24 or
  10.2.1.0/24 and die at the gateway; the backbone then ages out its LSAs
  and withdraws 10.200.0.0/24. Farm-internal L2 and the gateway address
  itself keep working (bridging and zebra are untouched), and pod-to-pod
  traffic never crosses this device.
Localization: switch_server_access
Root cause: ospfd not running on switch_server_access
Fix: restart FRR on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on switch_server_access" -- that is the same fault observed at
the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on switch_server_access (`service frr restart`).
The OSPF config lives in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process,
not the file), so a plain restart reloads it, 10.200.0.0/24 is re-advertised
into area 0, and both pods regain the server farm.
scoring_axes: bonus-rules-out-l2: notes farm-internal reachability and the 10.200.0.1 gateway still work, so the fault is L3/OSPF on switch_server_access, not the bridge or the servers

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The OSPF routing daemon (`ospfd`) on `switch_server_access` is not running and has no OSPF `network` statements configured. This device acts as the gateway (`10.200.0.1`) for the entire server-side segment (DNS server, web_server_0–3).

**Mechanism:** Without `ospfd` running or any configured OSPF network statements, `switch_server_access` never forms an OSPF adjacency with `router_core_3` over their shared point-to-point link (`172.16.0.10/31`, area 0.0.0.0). As a result, two things fail simultaneously: (1) the server subnet `10.200.0.0/x` is never advertised into the OSPF domain, so no upstream router learns how to reach the servers; and (2) `switch_server_access` itself has zero OSPF-learned routes, so it cannot forward packets toward user pod subnets `10.1.1.0/24` or `10.2.1.0/24`. Both halves of the cross-domain path black-hole: user pods receive ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" from `10.1.1.1` (switch_dist_1_1 — no route to server subnet), and servers receive the same from `10.200.0.1` (switch_server_access — no route to pod subnets).

**Localization:** `switch_server_access`, confirmed by `ospfd=no`, zero network statements, zero neighbors, and zero OSPF routes in the snapshot. `router_core_3:eth2` (the uplink to switch_server_access) confirms the other side of the broken adjacency with `adj=0`.

**Root cause:** `switch_server_access` is missing all OSPF configuration and its `ospfd` process is not running, severing the entire server segment from the OSPF routing domain.

**Fix:** Enable `ospfd` on `switch_server_access`, add OSPF `network` statements for `172.16.0.10/31` (area 0.0.0.0, matching router_core_3's peer config) and `10.200.0.0/x` (the server subnet), and restart FRR so the adjacency with `router_core_3` can form and routes propagate.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly localizes the fault to switch_server_access (ospfd not running/missing OSPF config).
The agent explicitly states ospfd on switch_server_access is not running (ospfd=no) and cites zero neighbors/routes, correctly identifying the OSPF daemon as down.
